@servers.sheet.usernamePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the username field of the sign-in sheet (when the server gave no hint about who signs in) and of the Add server sheet for SFTP and WebDAV. "barry" is a sample first name; swap it for a typical sample name in the target language if appropriate. The word before it is the ordinary label your language puts in front of an example.

servers.pinHint.title: Your Network group is getting long

@servers.pinHint.title.description: Title of a one-time notification, shown the first time five servers sit in the volume switcher's Network group. "Network group" is the heading in the switcher (the dropdown listing disks and servers) that servers are filed under; use the same wording as that heading. Friendly and factual, never a warning.

servers.pinHint.body: Right-click a server and choose Unpin from switcher, or use “{command}” from the command palette. It stays in the Servers list.

@servers.pinHint.body.description: Body of that notification: how to take a server out of the volume switcher, and the reassurance that unpinning loses nothing. "Unpin" must match the context-menu item menu.network.unpin word for word. "Servers" is the hub row in the switcher that lists every saved server. The command name arrives translated in {command}; keep the quotation marks your language uses around a UI label.

placeholders.command: the name of the command palette entry that pins or unpins a server, already translated

@servers.pinHint.gotIt.description: VERB phrase (imperative), the button that dismisses the notification. Casual acknowledgement, the way a person says "understood" and moves on. Two or three words at most.

@servers.hub.colName.description: Column heading in the servers hub: the server’s own name. One or two words; the column is narrow.

@servers.hub.colType.description: Column heading in the servers hub for which protocol a server speaks (SFTP, WebDAV, SMB). One word.

@servers.hub.colAddress.description: Column heading in the servers hub for where the server lives: a hostname, an IP address, or a web address. One word.

@servers.hub.colStatus.description: Column heading in the servers hub for how the server is doing right now. One word.

@servers.hub.colLastUsed.description: Column heading in the servers hub for when the user last connected to the server. Two words at most.

@servers.hub.addServer.description: The last row of the servers hub, which opens the form for typing a new server. VERB phrase, imperative. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026) and means "this opens something"; keep it.

@servers.hub.status.connected.description: Status of a server the app is talking to right now. One word, ADJECTIVE.

@servers.hub.status.saved.description: Status of a server the user has saved but isn’t connected to. Nothing is wrong; it’s simply idle. One word, ADJECTIVE.

@servers.hub.status.foundNearby.description: Status of a server Cmdr can see on the local network right now, whether or not the user saved it. Two words.

@servers.hub.status.signedOut.description: Status of a saved server whose session ended because a password is what’s missing. ❗ NOT a rejection and not a fault: the user simply has to sign in again.

servers.hub.status.waitingForKey: Waiting for you to check the key

@servers.hub.status.waitingForKey.description: Status of an SSH server whose identity key the user hasn’t approved yet. "The key" is the server’s SSH host key, a fingerprint a person compares before trusting the server. Address the user directly.

@servers.hub.neverUsed.description: Shown in the servers hub’s "Last used" column for a server the user has never connected to. One word.

@servers.hub.shareAccount.description: Shown after an SMB server's or saved share's name in the Servers list, and after the server's name in its share list, in a quieter color, saying which account it's signed in as: "Container as sven". {username} is the account name, never translated.

@servers.hub.guestAccount.description: Shown after an SMB server's or share's name in the Servers list, and after the server's name in its share list, in a quieter color: the server is signed in to as a guest, with no account. Pairs with servers.hub.shareAccount ("as sven"); keep the two built the same way.

servers.hub.editPickHint: Select a server to edit it.

@servers.hub.editPickHint.description: Toast when the user presses Edit or Rename (F4, F2) in the Servers list while the cursor is on the "Add server…" row rather than on a server.

servers.hub.editShareHint: A share has nothing to edit. To edit its server, select the server’s row.

@servers.hub.editShareHint.description: Toast when the user presses Edit or Rename (F4, F2) on a saved SMB share's row in the Servers list. Shares carry no settings of their own; the server row right above them does.

servers.hub.editNearbyHint: {name} was found nearby and isn’t saved, so there’s nothing to edit.

@servers.hub.editNearbyHint.description: Toast when the user presses Edit or Rename (F4, F2) on a server row in the Servers list that Cmdr only found on the local network and the user never saved. {name} is the server's name.

@servers.hub.s3AllBuckets.description: Name of a row in the Servers list, indented right under an S3 storage account’s row (which shows the account’s name): opening it shows every bucket that account can see. The other rows under the account are single buckets, shown by their own names. “Bucket” is the S3 term for a top-level storage container; use the term the providers’ consoles use in your language. Short, NOUN phrase, sentence case.

servers.hub.openAccountHint: {name} isn’t a place to open. Open one of the buckets under it.

@servers.hub.openAccountHint.description: Toast when the user presses Enter or double-clicks an S3 account’s row in the Servers list. The account itself can’t be opened; its saved buckets, listed as rows right below it, can. “Bucket” is the S3 term; keep the provider console’s term.

placeholders.name: the account’s name in the list, like "Photos backup"

servers.hub.forgetAccountConfirm: Forget {name} and every bucket saved under it? Cmdr drops their connections and stops listing them. Your files stay in the buckets.

@servers.hub.forgetAccountConfirm.description: Body of the confirmation dialog before an S3 account and all its saved buckets leave the Servers list and the volume switcher (F8 on the account’s row). Reassures that nothing in storage is deleted. “Bucket” is the S3 term; keep the provider console’s term.

placeholders.name: the account’s name in the list, like "Photos backup"

servers.hub.forgetSecretKeyToo: Also forget the account’s secret access key

@servers.hub.forgetSecretKeyToo.description: Checkbox in the Forget confirmation for an S3 account or one of its buckets: when checked, the secret access key Cmdr saved for the account is deleted too. Every bucket under the account uses that one key, so it’s unchecked when forgetting a single bucket. Same term as servers.sheet.secretAccessKey. Sentence case, no final period.

@servers.hub.forgetShare.description: VERB phrase. Item in a saved SMB share's right-click menu in the Servers list: drops the saved share from the list and the volume switcher. Match the wording of menu.network.forgetServer, with share in place of server.

@servers.hub.forgetShareConfirmTitle.description: Title of the confirmation dialog that asks before a saved SMB share leaves the Servers list.

servers.hub.forgetShareConfirm: Forget {name}? Cmdr stops listing it. If it’s mounted, it stays mounted, and your files stay on the server.

@servers.hub.forgetShareConfirm.description: Body of the confirmation dialog before a saved SMB share leaves the Servers list and the volume switcher. {name} is the share's name. Reassures that nothing is unmounted or deleted.

servers.hub.nearbyGroup: {count, plural, one {{countText} server found nearby} other {{countText} servers found nearby}}

@servers.hub.nearbyGroup.description: Header row in the servers hub, below the servers the user saved. It groups the servers Cmdr found on the local network that the user never saved, and it opens and collapses that group; collapsed, this line is all that shows of them. The rows under it carry the status "Found nearby", so use the same wording for "found nearby" here.

placeholders.count: the number of servers in the group, for choosing the plural form
placeholders.countText: the number as the user’s locale writes it, like "12"

@servers.hub.discoveryOff.description: One line in the servers hub, in place of the list of servers found nearby, when the user has turned local network discovery off in Settings. Saved servers still work and are still listed; this line is only about the nearby ones.

@servers.hub.discoveryOffLink.description: Link beside the discovery-off line; it opens Settings at the switch that turns local network discovery back on. VERB phrase, imperative. "Settings" is the app’s own Settings window; use the word your language’s macOS uses for it.

@servers.hub.emptyTitle.description: Heading of the empty state in the servers hub, when the user has saved none and Cmdr found none nearby. Short and neutral.

servers.hub.emptyMessage: Add one below, or turn on a Mac or NAS on your network and Cmdr will find it.

@servers.hub.emptyMessage.description: One line under the empty-state heading in the servers hub. "NAS" is a network storage box; keep the abbreviation if your language uses it, otherwise say the equivalent. "below" points at the "Add server…" row at the bottom of the list.

@servers.hub.rowCount.description: The count in the status bar under the servers hub. Counts saved servers and nearby ones together, and excludes the "Add server…" row.

placeholders.count: the number, for choosing the plural form
placeholders.countText: the number as the user’s locale writes it, like "1,024"

@servers.paneState.connecting.description: Heading of the pane view shown while Cmdr opens a connection to a server. {name} is the server’s display name. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026).
@servers.paneState.connecting.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.connectingHint: This can take a few seconds.

@servers.paneState.connectingHint.description: One line under the connecting heading, setting the expectation that a server handshake is not instant. Reassurance, not an instruction.
@servers.paneState.connectingHint.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.cancel.description: Button that calls off a connection Cmdr is in the middle of opening. VERB, imperative.
@servers.paneState.cancel.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.tryAgain.description: Button that starts the same connection over after it was refused. VERB phrase, imperative.
@servers.paneState.tryAgain.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.disconnect.description: Button that drops the server’s session and leaves the pane. VERB, imperative. A server has nothing to unplug, so it says Disconnect rather than Eject.
@servers.paneState.disconnect.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.refusal.authenticationRejected.description: Shown in the pane when the server refused the credential Cmdr offered. Factual, not accusing: the password may have changed on the server side.

placeholders.username: the account name on the server, like "ada"

servers.refusal.needsCredentials: This server asks for a password.

@servers.refusal.needsCredentials.description: Shown in the pane when the server wants a credential and Cmdr has none stored. ❗ NOT a rejection: nothing was ever offered, so don’t word it as a wrong password.

servers.refusal.accountNotPermitted: {username} doesn’t have access here. Try a different account.

@servers.refusal.accountNotPermitted.description: Shown in the sign-in sheet when the server accepted the account, but the place being opened (for example a network share) doesn’t let that account in. ❗ NOT a wrong password: the sign-in worked, so don’t word it as a rejected credential. "Here" is the place named in the sheet’s header.

placeholders.username: the account name on the server, like "ada"

servers.refusal.authMethodUnsupported: This server uses a sign-in method Cmdr doesn’t support yet.

@servers.refusal.authMethodUnsupported.description: Shown in the pane when the server challenged with an authentication scheme Cmdr doesn’t speak. The secret was never sent, so nothing about it is known to be wrong. ❌ Don’t name the scheme: it means nothing to the reader.

servers.refusal.certificateUntrusted: macOS doesn’t trust this server’s certificate. Add it in Keychain Access, then try again.

@servers.refusal.certificateUntrusted.description: Shown in the pane when a WebDAV server’s TLS certificate isn’t trusted by the operating system. "Keychain Access" is the macOS app name, which the OS ships translated; use the name your language’s macOS uses.

servers.refusal.notAWebdavServer: Nothing at this address answers WebDAV.

@servers.refusal.notAWebdavServer.description: Shown in the pane when the address answers as a web server but doesn’t speak WebDAV. "WebDAV" is a protocol name; don’t translate it.

servers.refusal.invalidUrl: That doesn’t look like a server address.

@servers.refusal.invalidUrl.description: Shown in the pane when the saved address isn’t a usable web address at all.

@servers.refusal.timedOut.description: Shown in the pane when the server didn’t finish the handshake inside Cmdr’s budget.

placeholders.host: the server’s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

@servers.refusal.unreachable.description: Shown in the Add server form and the sign-in form when there was no route to the server at all: it’s off, the name doesn’t resolve, or the network is down. Names the address the person typed (a pane standing on a saved server says servers.paneState.unreachable instead). "Cmdr" is the product name.

placeholders.host: the server’s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

servers.refusal.localNetworkHint: If the server is on, check that Cmdr is allowed under {localNetwork}.

@servers.refusal.localNetworkHint.description: A softer second line under "Cmdr couldn’t reach {host}." ("servers.refusal.unreachable") in the Add server form, shown only when this Mac itself refused the route to a local-network address. That is also how a stuck macOS Local Network privacy permission shows, but a server that’s switched off can look the same, so this only suggests checking. "Cmdr" is the product name.

placeholders.localNetwork: the OS-localized macOS "Local Network" permission name, as System Settings shows it under Privacy & Security, injected at runtime (it follows the Mac’s system language, which can differ from Cmdr’s, so it may arrive in English)

servers.refusal.hostKeyUntrusted: Cmdr hasn’t trusted the key for {host} yet.

@servers.refusal.hostKeyUntrusted.description: Shown in the pane when an SSH server presents a host key this Mac hasn’t approved. "Key" is the server’s SSH host key, the fingerprint a person checks before trusting the server.

placeholders.host: the server’s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

servers.refusal.hostKeyRevoked: The key for {host} is marked as compromised in your SSH settings on this Mac. Cmdr won’t connect to it.

@servers.refusal.hostKeyRevoked.description: Shown in the pane when the server’s SSH host key is listed as revoked in the user’s own known_hosts file. This one is deliberately final: there is no button that can safely undo it. "SSH" is a protocol name; don’t translate it.

placeholders.host: the server’s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

servers.refusal.startFolderOutsideRoot: The start folder has to be the root folder or a folder inside it.

@servers.refusal.startFolderOutsideRoot.description: Shown under the Start folder field of the add or edit server sheet when the typed start folder is neither the root folder nor a folder inside it. Nothing was saved or dialed. Calm and instructive. "Start folder" and "root folder" must use the same words as the field labels (servers.sheet.startFolder and servers.sheet.rootFolder).

servers.refusal.rootNotFound: Cmdr can’t open this folder on {host}. Check that it exists and that your account can read it.

@servers.refusal.rootNotFound.description: Shown under the Root folder field when the user saves an edit to a server that is connected right now, and the server has no folder at that path this account can open: it is missing, it is a file, or access is refused. Nothing was saved. "Cmdr" is the product name.

placeholders.host: the server’s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

servers.refusal.startFolderNotFound: Cmdr can’t open this start folder on {host}. Check that it exists and that your account can read it.

@servers.refusal.startFolderNotFound.description: Shown under the Start folder field when the user saves an edit to a server that is connected right now, and the server has no folder at the start folder path this account can open: it is missing, it is a file, or access is refused. Nothing was saved. "start folder" must match the servers.sheet.startFolder label. "Cmdr" is the product name.

placeholders.host: the server’s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

@servers.refusal.passwordMissing.description: Under the password field of the Add server sheet, when the field is empty and Cmdr has no saved password for this account, so nothing was sent to the server yet. {username} is the account name, never translated.

servers.refusal.saveUnconfirmed: {host} didn’t answer in time, so nothing was saved. Try again in a moment.

@servers.refusal.saveUnconfirmed.description: Shown above the buttons of the edit server sheet when saving needed the connected server to confirm a folder and it did not answer within a few seconds. Nothing was saved, and trying again is safe.

placeholders.host: the server’s hostname or address, like "nas.local"

servers.refusal.secretNotStored: Cmdr couldn’t store this password in your Keychain. Try again, or turn off “Remember in Keychain” to sign in without storing it.

@servers.refusal.secretNotStored.description: Shown under the password field of the sign-in sheet when the user turned on “Remember in Keychain” and the system’s password store refused to keep the password: the user clicked Deny on the system prompt, the keychain is locked, or no password store is available. Cmdr hasn’t tried to sign in yet, and nothing else changed. “Remember in Keychain” must match the servers.sheet.remember checkbox label word for word, inside the quotation marks your language uses. “Keychain” is Apple’s name for the password store; use the name your language’s macOS uses.

servers.refusal.savedSecretNotUpdated: Cmdr saved your changes but couldn’t update the password in your Keychain. Save again to try once more.

@servers.refusal.savedSecretNotUpdated.description: Shown under the password field of the edit server sheet when the server’s other settings were saved, but the system’s password store refused to keep or remove the password: the user clicked Deny on the system prompt, the keychain is locked, or no password store is available. ❗ The other changes DID save, so don’t word it as if nothing was saved. Pressing Save again is safe and only retries the password. “Save” is the sheet’s button (servers.sheet.save). “Keychain” is Apple’s name for the password store; use the name your language’s macOS uses.

servers.refusal.s3AuthenticationRejected: That secret access key didn’t work.

@servers.refusal.s3AuthenticationRejecte.description: Shown when an S3 storage server refused the secret access key Cmdr offered for this access key ID. Factual, not accusing. “Secret access key” is the credential name S3 providers use; match the provider console’s term in your language if it has one, and use the same words as servers.sheet.secretAccessKey.

servers.refusal.s3NeedsCredentials: This account asks for a secret access key.

@servers.refusal.s3NeedsCredentials.description: Shown when an S3 account wants its secret access key and Cmdr has none stored. ❗ NOT a rejection: nothing was ever offered, so don’t word it as a wrong key. Same term as servers.sheet.secretAccessKey.

@servers.refusal.s3SecretMissing.description: Under the secret access key field of the Add server sheet, when the field is empty and Cmdr has no stored key for this account, so nothing was sent yet. Same term as servers.sheet.secretAccessKey.

servers.refusal.s3SecretNotStored: Cmdr couldn’t store this secret access key in your Keychain. Try again, or turn off “Remember in Keychain” to sign in without storing it.

@servers.refusal.s3SecretNotStored.description: The S3 twin of servers.refusal.secretNotStored: the user turned on “Remember in Keychain” and the system’s password store refused to keep the key (Deny on the system prompt, a locked keychain, or no store). Nothing else changed. “Remember in Keychain” must match the servers.sheet.remember label word for word. “Keychain” is Apple’s name; use the name your language’s macOS uses.

servers.refusal.s3SavedSecretNotUpdated: Cmdr saved your changes but couldn’t update the secret access key in your Keychain. Save again to try once more.

@servers.refusal.s3SavedSecretNotUpdated.description: The S3 twin of servers.refusal.savedSecretNotUpdated: the edit DID save, and only writing the secret access key to the system’s password store didn’t. Pressing Save again is safe. “Save” is servers.sheet.save. “Keychain” is Apple’s name; use the name your language’s macOS uses.

servers.refusal.accessDenied: This key can’t reach this bucket. Check the bucket name and the secret access key, and that the key may read the bucket.

@servers.refusal.accessDenied.description: Under the secret access key field when an S3 bucket refused the key. The server can’t say whether the bucket name is mistyped (Cloudflare R2 answers this way for a bucket that doesn’t exist), the secret is wrong, or the key has no rights to this bucket, so the sentence asks about all three. “Key” is the S3 access key; “bucket” is the S3 term for a top-level storage container; keep the provider console’s terms.

servers.refusal.bucketListRefused: This key can’t list the buckets on this account. Type a bucket name to open that bucket, or check the secret access key.

@servers.refusal.bucketListRefused.description: Under the Bucket field when the user left it empty (which opens the whole account and lists its buckets) and the key isn’t allowed to list buckets. On some servers a wrong secret answers the same way, so it mentions both. “Bucket” is the S3 term; keep the provider console’s term.

servers.refusal.bucketNotFound: There’s no bucket by that name at {host}.

@servers.refusal.bucketNotFound.description: Under the Bucket field when the S3 server has no bucket with the typed name. “Bucket” is the S3 term; keep the provider console’s term.

placeholders.host: the storage server’s host name, like "s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com"

servers.refusal.regionMismatch: This bucket is in a different region. Pick its region and try again.

@servers.refusal.regionMismatch.description: Under the Region field when the S3 bucket lives in another region than the one chosen, and the server didn’t say which. “Region” must match servers.sheet.s3Region.

servers.refusal.regionMismatchNamed: This bucket is in {region}. Pick that region and try again.

@servers.refusal.regionMismatchNamed.description: Under the Region field when the S3 bucket lives in another region than the one chosen. “Region” matches servers.sheet.s3Region.

placeholders.region: a region code, like "us-east-2"; never translated

servers.refusal.clockSkewed: This Mac’s clock is off by more than 15 minutes, so the server won’t accept Cmdr’s requests. Set the date and time automatically in System Settings, then try again.

@servers.refusal.clockSkewed.description: Shown when an S3 server refused the request because this Mac’s clock is too far off: S3 signatures carry a timestamp. “System Settings” is the macOS app name; use the name your language’s macOS uses.

servers.refusal.notAnS3Endpoint: Nothing at this address answers as S3 storage.

@servers.refusal.notAnS3Endpoint.description: Under the endpoint field when the address answers as a web server but not as S3-compatible storage. “S3” is a protocol name; don’t translate it.

servers.refusal.s3FieldMalformed: Use only lowercase letters, digits, and dashes here.

@servers.refusal.s3FieldMalformed.description: Under the Region, Location, or Account ID field of the S3 form, before anything was sent, when the typed value holds other characters. Short and instructive.

servers.refusal.endpointMalformed: Enter the endpoint as http:// or https:// plus a host name, like https://s3.example.com.

@servers.refusal.endpointMalformed.description: Under the Endpoint field of the S3 form (“Other S3-compatible”), before anything was sent, when the typed value isn’t a web address made of a scheme, a host, and an optional port. Keep http://, https://, and the example address as they are.

servers.refusal.addressTaken: You already saved this address as {name}. Open that one instead, or forget it first to move this server here.

@servers.refusal.addressTaken.description: Under the Address field of the edit server sheet, when the user changed a saved server's address to one another saved server already uses. Nothing was saved. The user can either use the other saved server, or remove it and then save this edit again. “Forget” is the exact word on the menu item that removes a saved server (“Forget server”), so use the same word your translation uses there.

placeholders.name: what the OTHER saved server is called in the Servers list, like "Naspolya" or "ada@nas.local"

servers.refusal.secretNotMoved: Cmdr couldn’t take the saved password along to the new address, so nothing changed. Check that your Keychain is unlocked, then save again.

@servers.refusal.secretNotMoved.description: Under the password field of the edit server sheet, when the user changed a saved server's address and Cmdr couldn't copy its stored password to the new address (the user clicked Deny on the system prompt, the keychain is locked, or no password store is available). ❗ NOTHING was saved, not even the other changes, so don't word it as if anything was. Saving again is safe. “Keychain” is Apple’s name for the password store; use the name your language’s macOS uses.

servers.refusal.accountChanged: A different account is a different server, so nothing was saved. Add it as a new server instead.

@servers.refusal.accountChanged.description: Above the buttons of the edit server sheet, when a save asked to change which account or which protocol a saved server uses. The sheet doesn't let the user type either, so this is rare. Nothing was saved. “Add” refers to adding a server from the Servers list.

@servers.sheet.addTitle.description: Title of the sheet where the user types a new server. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.signInTitle.description: Title of the sheet when a server is asking for a credential. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.editTitle.description: Title of the sheet when the user is changing a server they already saved. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.addAndOpen.description: Primary button of the Add server sheet, and what Enter does: checks the server, saves it, and opens it in the pane. VERB phrase. Pairs with servers.sheet.add, which only saves.

@servers.sheet.add.description: Secondary button of the Add server sheet: checks the server and saves it to the Servers list without opening it. VERB, one word. Pairs with servers.sheet.addAndOpen.

@servers.sheet.addAnyway.description: Small button under the address in the Add server sheet, shown only after Cmdr couldn't reach the server: saves it as typed without checking anything. VERB phrase.

servers.sheet.addAnywayHelp: Cmdr couldn’t check this server, so Add anyway saves it as you typed it.

@servers.sheet.addAnywayHelp.description: One line beside the Add anyway button: nothing about the server was checked, so a typo would be saved too. "Add anyway" must match servers.sheet.addAnyway word for word.

servers.sheet.addedToast: {name} is saved in your Servers list.

@servers.sheet.addedToast.description: Success notification after the Add button saved a server without opening it, shown when the Servers list isn't on screen to show the new row. {name} is the server's name as the list shows it.

placeholders.name: the server's name, like Sven's NAS or 192.168.0.153

@servers.sheet.signIn.description: The sheet's main button when a server is asking for a credential. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.save.description: The sheet's main button when the user is editing a saved server. VERB, imperative.

@servers.sheet.cancel.description: The sheet's secondary button: it closes without connecting or saving. VERB, imperative.

@servers.sheet.connecting.description: Replaces the main button's label while the sheet is waiting for the server. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026).

@servers.sheet.protocolLegend.description: Accessible name of the SMB / SFTP / WebDAV picker in the add form. Screen readers only; not visible. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.protocolSmb.description: One option of the protocol picker. A protocol name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.protocolSftp.description: One option of the protocol picker. A protocol name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.protocolWebdav.description: One option of the protocol picker. A protocol name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.address.description: Label of the field where the user types where the server lives. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.addressPlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside the address field. A short example hostname; leave it as-is or use an equally short one.

servers.sheet.addressHelpSftp: A hostname, an address you copied, or a whole ssh line.

@servers.sheet.addressHelpSftp.description: One line under the address field while SFTP is the selected protocol, telling the user they can paste whatever they have. “ssh” is a command name, keep it lowercase and untranslated.

servers.sheet.addressHelpSmb: A hostname, an IP address, or an smb:// address you copied.

@servers.sheet.addressHelpSmb.description: One line under the address field while SMB is the selected protocol, telling the user what they can type or paste. “smb://” is a URL scheme, keep it as-is.

servers.sheet.addressHelpWebdav: A web address you copied, like https://nas.local/dav, or a hostname.

@servers.sheet.addressHelpWebdav.description: One line under the address field while WebDAV is the selected protocol, telling the user what they can type or paste. Keep the example URL as-is.

servers.sheet.addressLooksLikeSmb: This looks like an SMB address. Pick SMB above if that’s what you meant.

@servers.sheet.addressLooksLikeSmb.description: Warning under the address field in the "Add server" form, shown while the user types an address that looks like it's for SMB (for example it starts with smb://) but a different protocol is selected in the SMB / SFTP / WebDAV picker right above the field. Nothing changes on its own; the user decides. “SMB” is a protocol name; keep it as-is. “Pick” matches the picker's buttons, which are above this line.

servers.sheet.addressLooksLikeSftp: This looks like an SFTP address. Pick SFTP above if that’s what you meant.

@servers.sheet.addressLooksLikeSftp.description: Warning under the address field in the "Add server" form, shown while the user types an address that looks like it's for SFTP (for example it starts with sftp:// or ssh://, or ends in port 22) but a different protocol is selected in the SMB / SFTP / WebDAV picker right above the field. Nothing changes on its own; the user decides. “SFTP” is a protocol name; keep it as-is.

servers.sheet.addressLooksLikeWebdav: This looks like a WebDAV address. Pick WebDAV above if that’s what you meant.

@servers.sheet.addressLooksLikeWebdav.description: Warning under the address field in the "Add server" form, shown while the user types an address that looks like it's for WebDAV (for example it starts with https://) but a different protocol is selected in the SMB / SFTP / WebDAV picker right above the field. Nothing changes on its own; the user decides. “WebDAV” is a protocol name; keep it as-is.

servers.sheet.addressLocked: The address is what identifies this server. To use another one, forget this server and add it again.

@servers.sheet.addressLocked.description: Under the greyed-out Address field when editing a saved SMB server: why it can't be changed there. "Forget" matches the menu item "Forget server".

servers.sheet.accountLocked: The protocol and the account are what name this server. To use another account, add it as a new server.

@servers.sheet.accountLocked.description: Under the greyed-out Username field when the user is EDITING a saved SFTP or WebDAV server, explaining why the protocol (the SMB / SFTP / WebDAV / S3 picker) and the account can't be changed there, and what to do instead. The address above them CAN be changed, so don't say it can't. “Add” refers to adding a server from the Servers list.

servers.sheet.addressMoveHelp: Did the server move? Type its new address. Its favorites, open tabs, and saved password come along.

@servers.sheet.addressMoveHelp.description: One line under the Address field when the user is EDITING a saved SFTP or WebDAV server, saying they can type the server's new address (for example after a NAS got a new IP address) and that nothing tied to the server is lost: favorites pointing into it, tabs open on it, and the password stored for it all follow it to the new address.

@servers.sheet.username.description: Label of the account field. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.password.description: Label of the password field. One word, NOUN.

servers.sheet.secretKeptPlaceholder: Saved in Keychain. Leave empty to keep it.

@servers.sheet.secretKeptPlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside the empty Password field (or the Secret access key field, for S3 storage) of the Edit server sheet, when Cmdr already has that secret stored in the macOS Keychain. Cmdr never shows a stored secret, so the field is always empty; this says one is saved, and that leaving the field empty and pressing Save keeps it. “It” is the password or the key, whichever the field is for. “Keychain” is the macOS feature name; use the name your language’s macOS uses (same as in servers.sheet.remember). Short: it has to fit inside a text field.

@servers.sheet.smbUsernamePlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside the optional Username field of the Add server sheet when SMB is selected. One word saying the field may stay empty.

servers.sheet.smbUsernameHelp: Fill this in if your NAS needs an account. Cmdr asks for the password when you open a share.

@servers.sheet.smbUsernameHelp.description: One line under the optional Username field of the Add and Edit server sheets for an SMB server. With a username, Cmdr signs in as that account instead of browsing the server as a guest, and asks for the password only when the person opens a share. Friendly and short.

@servers.sheet.passphrase.description: Label of the field for the passphrase that unlocks an SSH key FILE, which is not the account's password. Two words.

@servers.sheet.remember.description: Checkbox that stores the password in the macOS Keychain. “Keychain” is the macOS feature name, which the OS ships translated; use the name your language's macOS uses.

@servers.sheet.connectionModeLegend.description: Accessible name of the guest-or-account choice for a share that allows both. Screen readers only; not visible.

@servers.sheet.connectAsGuest.description: One option: open the share without an account, which some servers allow. VERB phrase, imperative.

servers.sheet.signInWithCredentials: Sign in with a username and password

@servers.sheet.signInWithCredentials.description: The other option: open the share as a named account. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.sheet.advanced.description: A collapsed section holding the settings most people never change. One word, ADJECTIVE.

servers.sheet.name: Name

@servers.sheet.name.description: Label of the field for what to call this server in the app. One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.protocolS3.description: One option of the protocol picker in the Add server sheet: S3-compatible object storage (Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, and others). A protocol name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.s3Provider.description: Label of the dropdown in the Add server sheet, S3 selected, that picks the storage service (Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, and so on). One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderAws.description: One choice in the S3 Provider dropdown. A product name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderR2.description: One choice in the S3 Provider dropdown. A product name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderB2.description: One choice in the S3 Provider dropdown. A product name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderWasabi.description: One choice in the S3 Provider dropdown. A product name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderHetzner.description: One choice in the S3 Provider dropdown. A product name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderGcs.description: One choice in the S3 Provider dropdown. A product name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderDigitalOcean.description: One choice in the S3 Provider dropdown. A product name; keep it as-is.

servers.sheet.s3GcsKeyHelp: Sign in with an HMAC key from the Interoperability tab of your Cloud Storage settings.

@servers.sheet.s3GcsKeyHelp.description: One line under the S3 Provider dropdown when Google Cloud Storage is picked: the access key ID and secret it asks for are an HMAC key, made in the Google Cloud console under Cloud Storage › Settings › Interoperability. “HMAC”, “Interoperability”, and “Cloud Storage” are Google’s own terms: keep “HMAC” as-is, and use the console’s own wording in your language for the tab and the settings if it has one.

@servers.sheet.s3ProviderOther.description: The last choice in the S3 Provider dropdown: any other storage server that speaks the S3 protocol (a self-hosted MinIO or Garage, for example). Picking it asks for the server’s web address. “S3” is a protocol name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.s3Region.description: Label of the field in the S3 form where the user types the storage region, a code like eu-west-1. One word, NOUN. Use the term the providers’ consoles use in your language.

servers.sheet.s3RegionOptionalPlaceholde: Optional. Leave empty to use us-east-1

@servers.sheet.s3RegionOptionalPlacehold.description: Placeholder inside the Region field for “Other S3-compatible” storage, where the region is optional. Keep us-east-1 as-is: it’s a region code. Short: it has to fit inside a text field.

@servers.sheet.s3AccountId.description: Label of the field in the S3 form, Cloudflare R2 selected, where the user types their Cloudflare account ID. Use the term Cloudflare’s dashboard uses in your language.

servers.sheet.s3AccountIdHelp: The account ID on your Cloudflare R2 overview page.

@servers.sheet.s3AccountIdHelp.description: One line under the Account ID field (Cloudflare R2 selected) saying where to find it. “Cloudflare R2” is a product name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.s3Location.description: Label of the dropdown in the S3 form, Hetzner Object Storage selected, that picks the data center location (fsn1, nbg1, hel1). One word, NOUN.

@servers.sheet.s3Endpoint.description: Label of the field in the S3 form, “Other S3-compatible” selected, where the user types the storage server’s web address, like https://s3.example.com. One word, NOUN; use the term S3 tools use in your language.

@servers.sheet.s3PathStyle.description: Checkbox in the S3 form, “Other S3-compatible” selected, on by default: the bucket name goes in the web address’s path rather than in the host name. “Path-style” is the S3 term for it; keep it recognizable. Sentence case, no final period.

servers.sheet.s3PathStyleHelp: Most self-hosted servers, like MinIO and Garage, need this.

@servers.sheet.s3PathStyleHelp.description: One line under the “Use path-style addressing” checkbox. MinIO and Garage are product names; keep them as-is.

@servers.sheet.s3Bucket.description: Label of the field in the S3 form where the user may type a bucket name. “Bucket” is the S3 term for a top-level storage container; use the term the providers’ consoles use in your language. One word, NOUN.

servers.sheet.s3BucketHelp: Leave it empty to see every bucket. If your key is limited to one bucket, type its name.

@servers.sheet.s3BucketHelp.description: One line under the Bucket field of the S3 form, the field has no placeholder. An empty Bucket opens the whole account and lists its buckets, which works only when the access key may list them; a key made for a single bucket (common with Cloudflare R2 and AWS) can’t, so for that key the field is needed. Shown in the add and edit forms, and stays visible beside a refusal under the field. “Bucket” is the S3 term; keep the providers’ term. “Key” is the access key.

@servers.sheet.s3UseRegion.description: Button under the Region field when the bucket turned out to live in another region and the server said which. It switches the Region field to that region and tries again. VERB phrase, imperative.

placeholders.region: a region code, like "us-east-2"; never translated

@servers.sheet.accessKeyId.description: Label of the field in the S3 form where the user types the access key ID, the public half of an S3 key pair (like AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE). Use the term the providers’ consoles use in your language.

@servers.sheet.secretAccessKey.description: Label of the field in the S3 form and the S3 sign-in sheet where the user types the secret access key, the private half of an S3 key pair (it works like a password). Use the term the providers’ consoles use in your language.

@servers.sheet.examplePlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside an S3 form field, showing a sample value. The word before it is the ordinary label your language puts in front of an example: match the catalog’s usual “Example:” prefix, the one most other placeholders use.

placeholders.example: a sample value kept as-is, like a region code "eu-west-1", an access key ID, or a web address

servers.sheet.identityLockedS3: The provider, the access key ID, and the bucket are what name this place. Forget it and add it again to change them.

@servers.sheet.identityLockedS3.description: Two lines under the greyed-out S3 fields when the user is EDITING a saved S3 place, explaining why those can’t be typed in and what to do instead. The S3 twin of servers.sheet.identityLocked; “Forget” is the same word as there. “Bucket” is the S3 term; keep the providers’ term.

servers.sheet.identityLockedS3Account: The provider and the access key ID are what name this account. Forget it and add it again to change them.

@servers.sheet.identityLockedS3Account.description: Two lines under the greyed-out provider and access key ID fields when the user is EDITING a saved S3 storage account (opened from the account’s row in the Servers list, so the Name field above is the account’s name and there’s no bucket field). Explains why those can’t be typed in and what to do instead. The account twin of servers.sheet.identityLockedS3; “Forget” is the same word as in servers.sheet.identityLocked. “Access key ID” matches servers.sheet.accessKeyId.

@servers.sheet.namePlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside the Name field of the add and edit server sheets. {label} is what Cmdr calls the server when the field stays empty: its address for an SMB server (192.168.0.153), or the account and host for SFTP and WebDAV (ada@nas.local). Short: it has to fit inside a text field.

placeholders.label: what Cmdr calls the server by default, like 192.168.0.153 or ada@nas.local; never translated

@servers.sheet.rootFolder.description: Label of the field for the folder ON THE SERVER this saved server is limited to: Cmdr never shows anything above it. Two words, NOUN phrase. The refusal messages and the start folder help reuse this term, so keep it consistent.

servers.sheet.rootFolderHelp: Cmdr never goes above this folder on the server.

@servers.sheet.rootFolderHelp.description: One line under the Root folder field, explaining that the folder is a ceiling: Cmdr never navigates above it on the server. "Cmdr" is the product name.

@servers.sheet.startFolder.description: Label of the field for the folder a pane opens at when the user opens this server. It must be the root folder or a folder inside it. Two words, NOUN phrase.

servers.sheet.startFolderHelp: Where the server opens. Leave it empty to open the root folder.

@servers.sheet.startFolderHelp.description: One line under the Start folder field: it is where the server opens, and leaving it empty opens the root folder. "root folder" must use the same words as the servers.sheet.rootFolder label.

@servers.sheet.keyFile.description: Label of the field for the SSH private key file to sign in with. “Key” is an SSH key. Two words.

@servers.sheet.browse.description: Button beside the key-file field; it opens the system file picker. VERB, imperative. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026) and means “this opens something”; keep it.

@servers.sheet.useAgent.description: Checkbox letting Cmdr ask the running ssh-agent for a key. “ssh-agent” is a program name; keep it as-is.

@servers.sheet.autoReconnect.description: Checkbox letting Cmdr redial this server on its own when the connection drops. Shown in the server sheet and as a checkbox row in a saved SFTP or WebDAV server's row menu (the volume switcher and the servers list). VERB phrase, imperative.

servers.sheet.autoReconnectHelp: If the connection drops, Cmdr reconnects to this server on its own. This doesn’t make Cmdr connect at startup: it connects when you open the server in a pane.

@servers.sheet.autoReconnectHelp.description: Tooltip explaining the “Reconnect automatically” checkbox, shown from an info glyph beside it in the server sheet, and as the hover tooltip of the same checkbox row in a saved server's row menu. Its job is to correct a likely misreading: the switch only reconnects after a dropped connection, and does NOT make Cmdr connect to the server when the app starts. “pane” is one of the app's two side-by-side file lists.

@servers.sheet.autoReconnectInfoLabel.description: Screen-reader name of the info glyph beside the “Reconnect automatically” checkbox; activating it shows the explanation. Never visible on screen. Quote the checkbox label exactly as servers.sheet.autoReconnect translates it, so voice-control users can name it.

servers.sheet.needsStoredSecret: Reconnecting on its own needs a remembered password. Turn on “Remember in Keychain” and sign in once.

@servers.sheet.needsStoredSecret.description: Shown in the edit sheet when “Reconnect automatically” is on but nothing is stored, so it can never actually run. Says what to do about it.

@servers.sheet.tryNextcloudAddress.description: Button offered when a web address answers but doesn't speak WebDAV. It appends the path Nextcloud and ownCloud keep their files under. “Nextcloud” is a product name; keep it as-is. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.hostKey.firstContactTitle.description: Heading of the step where the user approves a server's SSH identity key the first time. Routine, not alarming.

placeholders.host: the server’s hostname or address, like “nas.local”

servers.hostKey.firstContactBody: Check the fingerprint below against the one the server’s owner gave you, then trust it.

@servers.hostKey.firstContactBody.description: One line under that heading. “Fingerprint” is the short string that identifies an SSH key; a person compares it character by character.

@servers.hostKey.changedTitle.description: Heading of the same step when the server presents a DIFFERENT key than the one already trusted. This one is serious: it can mean someone is in the middle.

placeholders.host: the server’s hostname or address, like “nas.local”

servers.hostKey.changedBody: This can mean the server was reinstalled, or that something is sitting between you and it. Check the fingerprint with the server’s owner before trusting it.

@servers.hostKey.changedBody.description: One line under the changed-key heading. Says both innocent and serious causes, and what to do first.

@servers.hostKey.changedDisclosure.description: A collapsed section holding the button that trusts a CHANGED key. Deliberately behind a click, so trusting one is never a reflex. First person: the user speaking.

@servers.hostKey.fingerprintLabel.description: Label above the SSH key's algorithm and fingerprint. Two words, NOUN phrase.

@servers.hostKey.trustAndConnect.description: Button that records a first-contact key and carries on connecting. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.hostKey.trustNewKey.description: Button that records a CHANGED key, behind the disclosure. VERB phrase, imperative.

@servers.paneState.signedOut.description: Heading of the pane view shown when a server's session ended because a password is what's missing. ❗ NOT a rejection and not a fault: the user simply has to sign in again.
@servers.paneState.signedOut.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.notConnected.description: Heading of the pane view shown when the user cancelled connecting to a saved server or share (for example, closed its sign-in form). A plain statement, NOT an error: nothing failed, the person chose not to connect yet.

placeholders.name: the place’s display name, like “private on localhost:11481”

@servers.paneState.notConnected.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.unreachable.description: Heading of the pane view shown when the user opened a saved server and there was no route to it at all: it’s off, its address doesn’t resolve, or the network is down. Names the server by the name the user gave it. A Try again button sits below. "Cmdr" is the product name.

placeholders.name: the name the user gave the saved server, like “Naspolya”, or its hostname, like “nas.local”, when it has no name

@servers.paneState.unreachable.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.goBack.description: Button that takes the pane back to where it was before it opened this server or share. VERB phrase, imperative.
@servers.paneState.goBack.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.signIn.description: Button that opens the form for signing in to the server again. VERB phrase, imperative. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026) and means “this opens something”; keep it.
@servers.paneState.signIn.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.hostKeyChanged.description: Heading of the pane view shown when an SSH server presents a different identity key than the one this Mac trusts. Serious: it can mean someone is in the middle. “Cmdr” is the product name.
@servers.paneState.hostKeyChanged.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.hostKeyChangedHint: Its key changed. That can mean the server was reinstalled, or that something is sitting between you and it. Check the new key before you connect again.

@servers.paneState.hostKeyChangedHint.description: One line under that heading, saying both innocent and serious causes and what to do. “Key” is the server’s SSH host key, the identity it proves itself with. A “Check the key” button (servers.paneState.checkHostKey) sits right below it and opens the screen that shows the new key; use the same word for “key” in both.
@servers.paneState.hostKeyChangedHint.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.checkHostKey.description: Button under the changed-key message in a file pane. It opens the sign-in sheet on its host-key step, which shows the server’s new SSH host key and its fingerprint, with that screen’s own choices to trust it or not. The button itself trusts nothing. VERB, imperative, short control label. “Key” is the same SSH host key as in servers.paneState.hostKeyChangedHint.
@servers.paneState.checkHostKey.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.reconnecting.description: Heading of the pane view shown while Cmdr keeps trying to bring back a server connection that dropped. ❗ NOT a first connection: the session existed and Cmdr is getting it back on its own. {name} is the server’s display name. The ellipsis is the single character … (U+2026).
@servers.paneState.reconnecting.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.signedOutNothingToAsk: This server signs in with a key rather than a password, so there’s nothing to type. Open it again to retry.

@servers.paneState.signedOutNothingToAsk.description: One line under the "Signed out" heading, shown instead of a Sign in button when the server proves itself with an SSH key or an agent identity rather than a password. Say plainly that there is nothing for the user to enter and what they can do instead. ❗ Not an apology and not a fault.
@servers.paneState.signedOutNothingToAsk.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.retryProgressAriaLabe.description: Accessibility label for the countdown progress bar showing how long until the next reconnect attempt.
@servers.paneState.retryProgressAriaLabe.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.retryNow.description: Button that triggers a reconnect attempt immediately.
@servers.paneState.retryNow.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.retryNowTooltip.description: Hover tooltip for the button that triggers a reconnect attempt right away instead of waiting.
@servers.paneState.retryNowTooltip.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.cancelCycleTooltip: Stop trying for now. The connection stays available. Switch back to retry.

@servers.paneState.cancelCycleTooltip.description: Hover tooltip for the button that pauses auto-reconnect while keeping the connection available to resume.
@servers.paneState.cancelCycleTooltip.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.disconnectCycleTooltip: Stop trying and disconnect from the server.

@servers.paneState.disconnectCycleToolti.description: Hover tooltip for the button that stops reconnecting and drops the server connection.
@servers.paneState.disconnectCycleToolti.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

servers.paneState.retryKeepsTrying: Will keep trying for a total of {duration}.

@servers.paneState.retryKeepsTrying.description: Reassurance line telling the user how long the auto-reconnect will keep trying. {duration} is a phrase like "60 seconds" or "2 minutes".

placeholders.duration: the total duration phrase, e.g. 60 seconds or 2 minutes

@servers.paneState.retryKeepsTrying.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.retryTotalSeconds.description: Total reconnect-cycle duration phrased in seconds, embedded in the "Will keep trying for a total of …" sentence.

placeholders.seconds: the number of seconds, for choosing the plural form
placeholders.secondsText: the same number as the user's locale writes it, like "1,024"

@servers.paneState.retryTotalSeconds.screenshotNote: Shown inside a file pane while it connects to a server: "Connecting…", "Signed out", a changed host key, or a "Reconnecting…" state with a countdown and Retry/Cancel controls. This shows the servers list those connections start from; your string appears in the pane, in the same network context.

@servers.paneState.retryTotalMinutes.description: Total reconnect-cycle duration phrased in minutes, embedded in the "Will keep trying for a total of …" sentence.
